taxonomic_note: Accepted as a species by major current authorities, but Texas native status is unresolved: POWO treats Texas as introduced while USDA GRIN and Flora of North America support native/southwestern-U.S. treatment.
look_here_first: Against Euphorbia dentata, ignore overall habit first and go straight to the underside leaf hairs, then fruit and mature seed. E. davidii has shorter, stiffer, strongly tapered hairs often arising from minute pustular bases, larger capsules, and larger angular seeds with irregular low tubercles.

project_inclusion.target_zone_status: AUTHORITY CONFLICT — USER APPROVED LEARNER INCLUSION
project_inclusion.range_basis: POWO treats Texas as introduced; USDA GRIN explicitly treats Texas as native, and FNA describes a native southwestern U.S./northern Mexico to southern Great Plains range. The project does not manufacture PASS or FAIL while that conflict remains.

approval_exception.reason: Learner inclusion is allowed while authority conflict remains explicit.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbia sect. Poinsettia: milky latex and cyathia; the dentata group is difficult enough that mature seed characters are often the safest species-level evidence.
morphology_keys.growth_form: Annual taprooted herb, typically erect to ascending; often more robust than E. dentata but habit overlaps.
morphology_keys.leaves: Mostly opposite, coarsely toothed, often more elliptic than E. dentata, but leaf shape overlaps too much to use alone.
morphology_keys.hairs: Abaxial hairs relatively short, stiff, and strongly tapered, often seated on minute pustular bases. This texture is one of the best non-seed clues against E. dentata.
morphology_keys.cyathium: Single yellow-green gland, broadly attached; opening oblong; appendages absent.
morphology_keys.fruit: Capsules broadly ovoid, about 2.9–3.3 × 4–4.8 mm, 3-lobed and usually glabrous; larger than in E. dentata.
morphology_keys.seed: Seeds black, brown, or pale gray, ovoid to triangular-ovoid, angular in cross section, about 2.4–2.9 × 2.2–2.9 mm, with low tubercles arranged irregularly or in faint transverse rows; caruncle about 0.9–1.1 mm.
best_field_traits: short stiff strongly tapered hairs beneath leaves
minute pustular bases often visible beneath hairs
larger broadly ovoid capsules, about 2.9–3.3 × 4–4.8 mm
seed tubercles irregular rather than evenly distributed
often more elliptic leaves, but this is supporting only
morphology_keys.comparison_training: E. davidii = stiff short hairs + larger capsule + larger angular irregularly lumpy seed. E. dentata = longer weak filiform hairs + smaller capsule + smaller rounded evenly finely tuberculate seed.

lookalike_matrix.Euphorbia davidii: shorter, stiffer, strongly tapered; often on minute pustular bases
low tubercles irregularly arranged or in faint transverse rows

comparisons.key_distinctions: Seed is the best tie-breaker. Angular, larger, irregularly tuberculate seed strongly favors E. davidii; rounded, smaller, evenly finely tuberculate seed favors E. dentata.
